title: ROUTINE DISCHARGE PROCESS
knowledge: Discusses guidelines for the discharge process of the patient in the ward.
Identify purpose and importance of knowing the guidelines of discharge process.
Discusses the proper step of discharging the patient.
skills: Review the nursing assessment of the discharge needs relating to the physician order check in the Oasis Program.
For Non – Saudi Patient to inform the Non Saudi Administrator for their discharge process.
Ensure appointment slip is prepared for Out-patient department with regards to follow up visit after discharge.
Check the discharge medications or home care medications.

Review the update teaching needs for the patient and family such as:
    a. Medication name, dose, time to be taken and its side effects
    b. Steps of special procedures (tepid sponge bath, random blood sugar monitoring via needle prick)
    c. Diet
    d. Next appoint and visit
Obtained signature from the husband, father, and adult brother before discharge especially for female patients.
Ensured that the patient obtained all his/ her valuables.
Accompany the patient to exit via wheelchair or stretcher safely.
Ensure that the patient is discharge in the Oasis Program.
Document fully in the Handover Notes, Nurses notes and in the census book.
attitude: Accept constrictive criticism as learning opportunity.
To be self-aware of limitation in knowledge and skills.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.

Ability to organize and facilitate a Reflection session in and on practice after the Standards in Ward Routine Discharge learning opportunity occurs and activates findings to improve future practice and response.

title: END OF LIFE
knowledge: States the nurse's role in the care of the dying patient.
Verbalizes psychological needs of the dying patient and family of the dying patient.
Verbalizes physical needs of the dying patient.
States the signs and symptoms of discomfort in the dying patient and nursing interventions for each.
Verbalizes spiritual needs of the dying patient and patient's family.
States the nurse's role in ensuring adequate pain management for the dying patient.
Verbalizes support required by patient's family after death and throughout the grief process.
States the nurse's role in the care of the dying patient.
skills: Demonstrates nursing care of the dying patient.
Demonstrates assessment of the pain and preparation and administration of drugs to relieve pain.
Demonstrates nursing interventions to relieve symptoms of discomfort experienced by the dying patient.
Demonstrates support for patient and family psychological, social and spiritual needs.
Documents assessments, interventions and care of the dying patient.
attitude: Provides respectful and responsive care to the dying patient by providing comfort and dignity.
Provides respect for the following needs: confidentiality, privacy, security, resolutions of complaints, counseling and communication.
